subject: Private hosting governance / hosting variance clearance request
messages:
From: Emma Cho <emma.cho@acme-biosys.com>
To: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
Cc: legal@acme-biosys.com
Date: Sat, 29 May 2027 13:18:00 +0000
Subject: Private deployment ask + audit scope / discount request

Hi Lauren,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Acme BioSystems is ready to move forward with a private deployment (dedicated, customer-managed VPC) but we have a few non-standard asks that we need written into contract and operational runbooks before procurement will sign:

- Data residency: all inference logs and model inputs must remain in our EU tenancy and cannot be replicated outside EU regions.
- Audit access: our internal audit team requires quarterly snapshots (read-only) of runtime logs for a 60-day retention window and a 48-hour live-review window twice per year. We cannot grant continuous host-level access.
- Network constraints: certificate-based VPN for admin ops, no persistent bastion access.
- Support SLA escalation: 30-minute P1 response; otherwise we will seek a credit.

Procurement will also ask for a commercial concession given the engineering integration work — they are requesting a 25% discount on list pricing with a 36-month committed term.

I attached our security questionnaire and SOW for your internal review. Can you confirm whether Redwood can meet these constraints as written or if you need an exec-level clearance?

Best,
Emma
Emma Cho
Head of IT Compliance, Acme BioSystems
emma.cho@acme-biosys.com
+44 20 7946 0812

Attachments: Acme_Security_Questionnaire.pdf, SOW-Acme-Private-Deploy_v2.docx

From: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai, aditya.rao@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 09:07:00 +0000
Subject: Fwd: Private deployment ask + audit scope / discount request

Team — forwarding Acme's asks. TL;DR: EU-only data residency, limited/periodic audit snapshots (no continuous host access), cert-based VPN, and a commercial request for 25% off for 36 months.

Notes / asks:
- Marissa: legal to review the SOW redline risk (they've asked for read-only snapshots + specific retention + a 48-hour live-review twice yearly). Any fatal indemnity/C2P problems?
- Vivek: can we operationally commit to quarterly snapshots and a 48-hour live-review without persistent host access? If we need any infra changes, rough cost and timeline?
- Aditya: security implications of the proposed audit flow and certificate-only admin; can we provide an attested process that meets Acme's ask?

Acme is pushing to sign quickly; procurement says they'll only approve if the discount is in contract. If this needs an exec clearance (discount >15% or carveouts to our standard audit controls), please flag.

Thanks — Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Enterprise Account Executive, Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.ai

---Original message attached---

From: marissa.cole@redwood.ai <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai, aditya.rao@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 31 May 2027 11:44:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Fwd: Private deployment ask + audit scope / discount request

Lauren / team,

Reviewed the SOW and the security questionnaire. High-level legal points:

- Audit scope: We can accept read-only snapshots and a scheduled live-review, but we must carve language limiting the frequency and scope (e.g., two scheduled live-review events per 12 months; snapshots provided within 5 business days of request). Continuous host-level access or arbitrary forensic access is a no-go from our side.
- Data residency: we can contractually warrant that logs and customer data will be kept in EU-hosted storage, but need a defined failover policy if EU capacity is constrained.
- Indemnity / liability: Acme is asking to broaden indemnities tied to third-party claims resulting from their use. We should hold to our standard indemnity template and offer an additional security SLA credit in lieu of expanded indemnity.
- Pricing concession: legal does not approve contract-level pricing decisions; that goes to Deal Desk/Revenue Ops and requires exec signoff for discounts >15% for multi-year deals.

I've attached a redline of the SOW (SOW-Acme-Private-Deploy_redline.docx) highlighting the audit/indemnity sections. Operational controls will need precise language — Vivek and Aditya please review the suggested operational limits.

Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Attachments: SOW-Acme-Private-Deploy_redline.docx

From: vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, aditya.rao@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 13:02:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Fwd: Private deployment ask + audit scope / discount request

Quick operational summary from infra:

- Data residency: we can pin logs and storage to an EU-only tenancy and replicate only for DR within EU regions. We'll add a documented failover policy that requires customer opt-in before cross-region replication.
- Audit approach: we can provide quarterly read-only snapshots of the runtime logs (delivered as encrypted archives to an Acme-owned bucket) and support two scheduled 48-hour live-review windows per year during which we provide ephemeral access to aggregated telemetry and redacted traces. We cannot provide host-level interactive shells.
- Access model: certificate-based VPN + short-lived certificates (max 12h) for admin ops; all actions go through our RBAC and are logged. No persistent bastion will be provided.
- Effort & timeline: small infra config + SRE runbook updates; estimate 3–4 weeks to implement and test.

Commercial note: the Acme ask for a 25% concession is above our standard thresholds. From an infra POV: we can accept the operational constraints with the controls above, but discount beyond 15% requires exec signoff. If deal desk wants to push for 25%, we should tie it to a longer commit (48 months) or an onboarding fee to offset the one-time engineering work.

I'm happy to sign off on the technical approach and hand this to Deal Desk if we can get a commercial decision on the discount and the indemnity framing from Legal.

Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Infrastructure & Product Ops, Redwood Inference
vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai

From: aditya.rao@redwood.ai <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 20:22:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Fwd: Private deployment ask + audit scope / discount request

Marking this for executive clearance. Summary and recommendation:

- Security: proposed model (EU-only storage, encrypted snapshots, certificate-only admin, RBAC and short-lived certs) meets our baseline and minimizes blast radius. I have no technical objection to the operational carveouts described by Vivek.
- Legal: Marissa's redline limits the audit scope appropriately. We should include an audit playbook appendix (who gets access, what is redacted, SLAs for snapshot delivery).
- Commercial / Deal Desk: recommend a one-time engineering onboarding fee (we propose €60k) + a 15% list discount for a 36-month committed term. Approving anything above 15% or granting continuous host access would need an exec-level commercial concession (CMO/CFO approval).

If Leadership approves the 15% + €60k approach, I approve moving forward operationally and legal can finalize language per Marissa's redline. If Sales wants to accept the customer's 25% ask, please route to execs: Ashwin (CRO) and Priya (CFO) for a final concession call.

Aditya Rao
Head of Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.ai

Cc: Lauren — please capture this as the recommended deal motion in HubSpot and request an exec exception if Acme refuses the 15% + onboarding fee path.
